notes.front: What is MySQL?
notes.back: An open-source relational database management system that began as a simple-to-use system and is widely used for web applications.
notes.explanation: Its free Community edition has long been a popular choice for web applications running on Linux.
notes.example: Like a well-known, free recipe that thousands of small restaurants cook from, with paid versions sold to chains that want extra support.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “What are MySQL and PostgreSQL?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is a Linux, Apache, MySQL, and PHP (LAMP) stack?
notes.back: A common set of software for web applications: Linux, the Apache web server, the MySQL database and the PHP language.
notes.explanation: MySQL is the leading open-source relational database for applications built on this stack.
notes.example: Like a standard kitchen fit-out of oven, hob, fridge and sink: one familiar set of parts that many web builders install together.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “What are MySQL and PostgreSQL?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is PostgreSQL?
notes.back: A hybrid relational-object database: it stores data in relational tables but also allows custom data types with nonrelational properties.
notes.explanation: It is also extensible, so code modules can be added to the database and run by queries.
notes.example: Like a filing cabinet that also has drawers you can reshape for odd-sized items, such as maps and rolled plans.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “What are MySQL and PostgreSQL?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is pgsql?
notes.back: PostgreSQL’s own query language: a variant of standard SQL with features for writing stored procedures that run inside the database.
notes.explanation: It is PostgreSQL’s counterpart to T-SQL in Microsoft’s products.
notes.example: Like a regional dialect of English: anyone who knows the standard language follows most of it, but some words are local.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “What are MySQL and PostgreSQL?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is Azure Database for MySQL?
notes.back: A fully managed relational database service in Azure, based on the MySQL Community Edition database engine.
notes.explanation: It gives granular control and flexibility over database management functions and configuration settings.
notes.example: Like leasing a car with servicing included: you drive it, the leasing firm keeps it maintained.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn: Azure Database for MySQL flexible server overview, “Overview”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is Azure Database for PostgreSQL?
notes.back: A fully managed PostgreSQL database service in Azure that gives granular control over management functions and configuration settings.
notes.explanation: It offers the same kinds of availability, performance, scaling, security and administration benefits as the MySQL service.
notes.example: Like a serviced office furnished to your own layout: the building manager runs the building, but you arrange the rooms.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn: What is Azure Database for PostgreSQL?, “Overview”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: For Azure Database for MySQL and PostgreSQL, what is flexible server?
notes.back: A fully managed deployment option that gives finer control over database management functions and configuration settings, with cost optimisation controls.
notes.explanation: It combines a managed service with more say over how the server is set up.
notes.example: Like a hotel suite where you choose the room temperature, cleaning times and checkout hour, while the hotel still runs everything.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is pgAdmin?
notes.back: A familiar tool for managing and monitoring PostgreSQL databases, which can also connect to Azure Database for PostgreSQL.
notes.explanation: Existing PostgreSQL users can keep the tool they know after moving to Azure.
notes.example: Like keeping your usual email app after your company moves its mail server to a new provider.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “Benefits of Azure Database for PostgreSQL”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is the main reason Azure offers managed services for MySQL and PostgreSQL?
notes.back: So organisations using them in on-premises applications can move to Azure quickly, without significant changes to those applications.
notes.explanation: An application written for MySQL or PostgreSQL keeps talking to the same kind of database after the move.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “Describe Azure services for open-source databases”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Azure service runs MySQL as platform as a service?
notes.back: Azure Database for MySQL.
notes.explanation: It is one of Azure’s managed services for open-source relational systems, alongside the PostgreSQL service.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “Azure Database for MySQL”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Azure service runs PostgreSQL as platform as a service?
notes.back: Azure Database for PostgreSQL.
notes.explanation: It sits alongside the MySQL service as Azure’s other managed open-source relational offering in the training.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “Azure Database for PostgreSQL”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A charity’s on-premises booking system is built on PostgreSQL. It wants to move to Azure quickly without rewriting the application or managing servers. Which service fits?
notes.back: C: Azure Database for PostgreSQL.
notes.choices:
A) Azure SQL Database
B) Azure Database for MySQL
C) Azure Database for PostgreSQL
D) PostgreSQL installed on Azure Virtual Machines
notes.choicesExplained: A and B: moving to a different database system would mean changing the application. D: it runs PostgreSQL, but the charity would still manage the servers.
notes.explanation: The managed PostgreSQL service exists so that applications like this can move without significant changes.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “Describe Azure services for open-source databases”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which MySQL edition is free of charge?
notes.back: The Community edition; the Standard and Enterprise editions are paid for.
notes.explanation: The paid editions are the ones commercial organisations use most, though the free one has long been popular for web applications.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “What are MySQL and PostgreSQL?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which MySQL edition offers the fullest set of tools and features, including enhanced security, availability and scalability?
notes.back: The Enterprise edition.
notes.explanation: Standard adds higher performance and different storage technology; Enterprise goes further with its tooling.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “What are MySQL and PostgreSQL?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A small agency builds its client websites on Linux, Apache and PHP, and needs a free relational database to complete the stack. Which system is the usual choice?
notes.back: D: MySQL, using its free Community edition.
notes.choices:
A) PostgreSQL with pgsql extensions
B) Azure SQL Managed Instance
C) MySQL Enterprise edition
D) MySQL Community edition
notes.choicesExplained: A: PostgreSQL is a relational database, but the stack’s “M” is MySQL. B: a managed SQL Server instance is not part of the stack and is not free. C: Enterprise is a paid edition.
notes.explanation: MySQL is the leading open-source relational database for this stack of software.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “What are MySQL and PostgreSQL?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Besides relational tables, what else can a PostgreSQL database store?
notes.back: Custom data types with their own nonrelational properties.
notes.explanation: That is what makes it a hybrid relational-object database rather than a purely relational one.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “What are MySQL and PostgreSQL?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What kind of data can PostgreSQL store and manipulate as a key feature, such as lines, circles and polygons?
notes.back: Geometric data.
notes.explanation: Shapes can be kept and worked on inside the database, not only numbers and text.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “What are MySQL and PostgreSQL?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does it mean that PostgreSQL is extensible?
notes.back: You can add code modules to the database, and queries can run them.
notes.explanation: Extensions let a database take on specialised tasks beyond the built-in features.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “What are MySQL and PostgreSQL?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A mapping app must store delivery zones as polygons and query them inside the database, alongside ordinary relational tables. Which open-source system suits it better?
notes.back: B: PostgreSQL.
notes.choices:
A) MySQL Community edition
B) PostgreSQL
C) MySQL, because it is used in LAMP stacks
D) Neither: relational systems cannot hold shapes
notes.choicesExplained: A and C: the training names storing and manipulating geometric data as a key PostgreSQL feature, and makes no such claim for MySQL. D: PostgreSQL stores geometric data alongside its relational tables.
notes.explanation: Storing and manipulating geometric data such as polygons is one of PostgreSQL’s key features.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “What are MySQL and PostgreSQL?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Azure Database for MySQL flexible server, what do you pay for when you configure high availability?
notes.back: The compute and storage of both the primary and the standby replica that the service provisions.
notes.explanation: Turning on high availability makes the service create and manage a standby replica for automatic failover.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn: Azure Database for MySQL flexible server overview, “High availability within and across availability zones”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Azure Database for MySQL flexible server, what does the service patch automatically?
notes.back: The underlying hardware, the operating system and the database engine.
notes.explanation: You can let the system choose when patching happens or set your own maintenance window.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn: Azure Database for MySQL flexible server overview, “Automated patching with a managed maintenance window”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How long can Azure Database for MySQL flexible server keep automatic backups for point-in-time restore?
notes.back: You can set a retention period of 1 to 35 days; the default is seven days.
notes.explanation: A restore can go back to any moment inside whatever retention period you set.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn: Azure Database for MySQL flexible server overview, “Automatic backups”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: An auditor requires that a shop’s Azure Database for MySQL flexible server can be restored to any moment in the past 30 days. The server uses the default settings. What must change?
notes.back: C: raise the backup retention period from its seven-day default to at least 30 days.
notes.choices:
A) Nothing: the default keeps 35 days
B) It cannot be done: the maximum is 14 days
C) Raise the retention period to at least 30 days
D) Move to MySQL on a virtual machine
notes.choicesExplained: A: the default is seven days, not 35. B: the maximum is 35 days. D: the managed service can already meet the requirement.
notes.explanation: Retention can be set anywhere from 1 to 35 days, so 30 days fits but the default does not.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn: Azure Database for MySQL flexible server overview, “Automatic backups”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: For new Azure Database for MySQL workloads, which deployment option does Microsoft’s training recommend?
notes.back: Flexible server.
notes.explanation: It gives finer control over management and configuration, along with controls for keeping costs down.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A team is creating a new MySQL workload on Azure and wants a managed service with control over configuration and costs. What should they choose?
notes.back: C: Azure Database for MySQL, flexible server.
notes.choices:
A) Azure SQL Database
B) Azure Database for PostgreSQL
C) Azure Database for MySQL, flexible server
D) MySQL on a desktop computer in the office
notes.choicesExplained: A and B: they run different database systems, so the MySQL workload would need changes. D: that is neither managed nor in Azure.
notes.explanation: Flexible server is the recommended deployment option for new workloads and includes cost optimisation controls.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: With an Azure free account, how long can you use Azure Database for MySQL flexible server free of charge?
notes.back: Twelve months, within monthly usage limits.
notes.explanation: The training says the same 12-month free use applies to the PostgreSQL flexible server.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn: Azure Database for MySQL flexible server overview, “Free 12-month offer”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Why are certain operations unavailable in Azure Database for MySQL?
notes.back: They concern security and administration of the database server itself, which Azure manages.
notes.explanation: A managed service takes over the server, so some server-level tasks are no longer yours to perform.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “Azure Database for MySQL”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which features of on-premises PostgreSQL may be missing from Azure Database for PostgreSQL?
notes.back: Some extensions, such as writing stored procedures in languages other than pgsql, or interacting directly with the operating system.
notes.explanation: A core set of the most-used extensions is supported, and the list is kept under review.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “Azure Database for PostgreSQL”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: When you connect pgAdmin to Azure Database for PostgreSQL, what kind of task is not available?
notes.back: Server-focused tasks, such as backing up and restoring the server.
notes.explanation: Microsoft manages and maintains the server, so those jobs are no longer done through pgAdmin.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “Benefits of Azure Database for PostgreSQL”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Where does Azure Database for PostgreSQL record information about the queries run on a server?
notes.back: In a database named `azure_sys`, which you read through the `query_store.qs_view` view.
notes.explanation: Seeing which queries users run helps when you need to fine-tune an application’s queries.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “Benefits of Azure Database for PostgreSQL”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is the default backup retention period in Azure Database for PostgreSQL, and how far can it be extended?
notes.back: Seven days by default, and up to 35 days if you configure it.
notes.explanation: You can restore the server to any point within that retention period.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn: What is Azure Database for PostgreSQL?, “Automatic backups”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does Azure Database for PostgreSQL build in to keep the service highly available?
notes.back: Failure detection and failover mechanisms.
notes.explanation: High availability is part of the service rather than something you assemble yourself.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “Benefits of Azure Database for PostgreSQL”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How is Azure Database for MySQL priced, according to the training?
notes.back: Pay-as-you-go pricing, so you pay only for what you use.
notes.explanation: The training lists this among the service’s benefits, alongside built-in high availability and easy scaling.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “Benefits of Azure Database for MySQL”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What monitoring do Azure Database for MySQL servers provide?
notes.back: You can add alerts and view metrics and logs.
notes.explanation: The training lists monitoring among the benefits of the managed service.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “Benefits of Azure Database for MySQL”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In the training’s list of Azure Database for MySQL benefits, in which two states is data secured?
notes.back: At rest and in motion.
notes.explanation: Stored data and data travelling over the network are both protected.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “Benefits of Azure Database for MySQL”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A small firm runs MySQL on its own server and spends evenings patching the operating system and checking backups. Which change removes most of that work?
notes.back: D: moving to Azure Database for MySQL, which patches and backs up automatically.
notes.choices:
A) Install pgAdmin on the current server
B) Move MySQL onto Azure Virtual Machines
C) Buy a second on-premises server
D) Move to Azure Database for MySQL
notes.choicesExplained: B: on a virtual machine the firm still patches the operating system and manages backups itself. C: a second server doubles the work. A: pgAdmin is a PostgreSQL management tool and automates nothing.
notes.explanation: The managed service handles patching of hardware, operating system and engine, and takes automatic backups.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “Benefits of Azure Database for MySQL”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: MySQL versus PostgreSQL: how does the training characterise each?
notes.back: MySQL: a simple-to-use open-source system, leading for LAMP web apps. PostgreSQL: a hybrid relational-object database with custom types.
notes.explanation: Both are relational database management systems, each tailored for different specialisations.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training, Explore relational database services in Azure: Describe Azure services for open-source databases, “What are MySQL and PostgreSQL?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words
